body: nitpick, `p_ovewrite` -> `p_overwrite`

This seems to be the code that's already done in the advanced importer for making external textures external.

I do like directly exposing this feature as two top level import flags.

Maybe we can reuse that external texture machinery.

`Node *_post_fix_node(Node *p_node, Node *p_root, HashMap<Ref<ImporterMesh>, Vector<Ref<Shape3D>>> &collision_map, Pair<PackedVector3Array, PackedInt32Array> &r_occluder_arrays, HashSet<Ref<ImporterMesh>> &r_scanned_meshes, const Dictionary &p_node_data, const Dictionary &p_material_data, const Dictionary &p_animation_data, float p_animation_fps, float p_applied_root_scale, bool p_extract_mat, bool p_ovewrite, const String &p_path);` is a very long function. `bool p_extract_mat, bool p_ovewrite, const String &p_path` aren't the only type of resource that can be extracted. We can also extract materials, meshes and animations (Maybe any multi-resource.)
See https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/75924

> This seems to be the code that's already done in the advanced importer for making external textures external.

Actual extraction code is two lines, not sure if it is worth to make it shared, `advanced importer` is UI for it (target directory selection, and dialog asking which files to keep/overwrite), but normal import supposed to be fully automated and should not have any UI.
What I mean is somehow keep this pull request's 1 enum but try to extract common code.
Good point.

The existing "extract materials" action from the advanced import dialog creates `.[t]res` files, not `.material` files. Would it be more reasonable for this to _also_ make `.[t]res` files, so that both modes of automatic material extraction end up with the same result?
Yes
Changed it to `[t]res`.

> We can also extract materials, meshes and animations (Maybe any multi-resource.)

I'll keep it for material only for now, if there's demand for mesh and animation bulk extraction it can be added in a separate PR. Meshes and animations seems to be handled quite differently form materials.

use_external/path should be the uid:// path and fallback_path should be res://

the fact that we now have effectively duplicate code (with SceneImportSettingsDialoh) for extracting materials has me a little worried that there will be a divergence in behavior between the two (such as this uid assignment code as an  example)
Same problem: should handle fallback_path in caae the uid was lost and we need to lookup by res://
Same problem: should write fallback_path in caae the uid was lost and we need to lookup by res:// . Another case of duplicate logic which implies more maintenance burden

The only duplicate code is `ResourceSaver::save(md.material, path);` the rest can't be extracted since `SceneImportSettingsDialog` and `ResourceImporterScene` are using different data types to store metadata.
Added "UID" and `fallback_path` handing.

fallback_path should not be a UID path.

```suggestion
							matdata["use_external/fallback_path"] = path;
```

body: As for binary formats, I prefer allowing `.material` instead of `.res` just like in 3.x, because it's more semantically obvious what type of binary resource it is. I feel if we are adding this to improve compatibility with godot 3.x workflow, then the option should be .material. Or if we have disagreement, we could allow both .res and .material and let the user decide.

The default for extract_format should be 0 (text resources).

Note that Godot 4 extracts textures into seprarate files, so it is expected that materials be small. Having them in text formats makes working with version control easier.
